correctness.rationale: The flow is the negative gradient of a finite-dimensional convex edge p-energy. Every active direction-i edge lies in a complete coordinate fiber, giving the exact scalar factor 2+(q_i-2) alpha_p. Pairing all neighbors in each other coordinate gives a nonpositive contribution because the flux is monotone and their matched coordinate-i edge gap cannot exceed the active gap. Finite-max Dini comparison yields the all-time scalar profile, with zero-coordinate absorption by symmetry. The explicitly constructed separable initial data solve the full nonlinear ODE and attain equality for every coordinate and every time, including the sharp last-coordinate extinction time for 1<p<2. The standalone code independently reconstructed the vector field, passed 2265 exact active-edge inequalities and 54 exact extremizer identities, and checked 80 independently integrated flows; finite checks are corroboration only. The p=1 and variable-within-axis-weight cases are excluded.

originality.rationale: The principal nontrivial statement concerns axiswise sharpness and nonlinear product tensorization for d>=2. A one-clique local factor and p=2 Hamming heat are antecedents. Available earlier source results concern vertex-norm contraction, time regularity/extinction, linear gradient estimates, or discrete-time linear Hamming heat kernels, none of which specifies the optimal directional edge seminorm envelope or a single initial datum saturating all directions for every t. Related earlier mathematical records on product variation contraction or edge projection norms concern different operators. Similarity search did not reveal a dominating theorem, but absence from indexed sources does not prove priority.

value.rationale: The motivating gap is that nonlinear p-heat on a Cartesian graph product does not enjoy linear semigroup tensor-product superposition for arbitrary data, so coordinatewise sharp decay cannot be inferred from one-factor estimates or graph-wide vertex contraction. The theorem yields for every product size and anisotropic conductance the exact optimal time-evolution envelope for each directional edge gradient, proves simultaneously attainable sharpness using a new structural separation argument, and gives the optimal finite-time consensus bound for 1<p<2. This is a natural complete classification over an infinite graph family, useful for anisotropic nonlinear diffusion, not an arbitrary finite computation or renaming of the d=1 result.
